001.alt: Two line drawings show a woman gently squeezing a lemon into a bowl, then pressing its flattened rind.
001.caption: Gentle pressure gives juice; pressing the rind too far brings bitterness. An interpretation of the saying.

020.alt: A person examines a small stone through a loupe, with two similar-looking objects on the table.

034.alt: Milk foams over a metal pot and spills down a clay hearth.

037.alt: A woman’s feet and ankles, with simple anklets, remain visible beneath a hanging bordered sari.

049.alt: A tiny seed casts an exaggerated, enormous shadow.

061.alt: An iron rod is heated directly above charcoal embers, with its exposed ends extending beyond the heat.

065.alt: A small lizard follows a short curved track toward a bush.

073.alt: A line drawing sets a visible forest fire beside a woman quietly carrying grief.
073.caption: Visible fire and private grief are set beside each other as an interpretation of the saying.

075.alt: A richly dressed young royal figure receives khaja sweets.
075.caption: An imagined royal figure and sweet illustrate the saying; this is not a documented historical scene.

081.alt: A gust of wind takes the shape of a tiger beside a folded shawl.
081.caption: Winter’s bite takes the shape of a tiger. An interpretation of the metaphor, not a literal scene.

103.alt: A river curves through fields, trees and small houses.

106.alt: A flower floats in empty sky, its stem ending far above the ground.
106.caption: A beautiful flower, with nowhere to take root. An interpretation of the metaphor.

153.alt: A palm tree has upright and drooping fronds, with one dry frond falling.

050.alt: A woman applies oil to another woman’s already smoothly arranged hair.
